findings.message: The 052 expiry rule is now applied when the write runs, but not when the card is proposed. rotate_secret checks the rule in `propose` too (apps/web/lib/admin/secrets.ts:52-56), so a past expiry is refused before anyone types the value. set_github_app's `propose` only checks `clientId`, so an expired app still gets a confirm card. The person types the Client secret, confirms, and only then is refused with 'has passed; give a new expiresAt'. The same card also tells them the expired credential's 'old secret works 72 more hours', which isn't true for an expired credential. Fix: in `propose`, when `appRow` returns a row and no `expiresAt` was given, call `keptExpiryOf` and pass any error through `asRefusal`. Drop the 72-hours wording when the row is expired. Add the expired-without-expiresAt case to the expiry-116 table as a `propose` refusal.
findings.scenario: github-oauth expired on 2026-11-01. An Admin clicks the suggested 'Set up the GitHub app' and the card 'Replace the GitHub app' says 'the old secret works 72 more hours'. They paste the 40-character secret and confirm. The run is refused with 'the github-oauth credential's expiry (2026-11-01) has passed; give a new expiresAt', so the secret they typed is thrown away. With rotate_secret, the same state is refused before the card opens.

findings.message: set_github_app's `expiresAt` copies two pieces of secrets.ts: the `day` schema (regex and description, apps/web/lib/admin/secrets.ts:9) and `endOf` (`T23:59:59Z`, secrets.ts:22). The 'end of that day, UTC' meaning now lives in two places. Fix: export one day schema and one end-of-day helper from @amax/core/secrets and use them in both tools.

The docs no longer match the code. AC-2 and T2's guard bullet (line 98) still say put_secret and rotate_secret refuse a github-oauth value 'without one colon'. They now refuse github-oauth outright, whatever the value. AC-1 also doesn't mention the new `expiresAt` input, or that a past expiry is refused on replace. Update AC-1, AC-2 and T2 to match.
